Both **Monzo** and **Starling** are fully licensed UK banks protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS up to £85,000), and both consistently outrank traditional high-street banks for customer satisfaction. 

However, they cater to slightly different types of users:

---

### Key Comparison

| Feature | **Starling Bank** | **Monzo** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Philosophy** | A free, traditional bank rebuilt for smartphones (clean, straightforward, completely fee-free). | A feature-packed tech and budgeting app (vibrant, social, with paid tiers for extras). |
| **Spending Abroad** | **Mastercard rate, 0% fees.** | **Mastercard rate, 0% fees.** |
| **ATM Withdrawals Abroad** | **Unlimited fee-free withdrawals** anywhere worldwide (subject to daily £300 limit). | Fee-free in the EEA; **capped at £200/30 days** outside the EEA on the free tier (3% fee thereafter). |
| **Cash Deposits** | **Free at the Post Office** up to £1,000 per calendar year (0.7% fee thereafter). | **£1 fee per deposit** at PayPoint or the Post Office (free tier). |
| **Cheque Deposits** | In-app photo scanning up to £1,000; free post for larger amounts. | In-app photo scanning (or postal service). |
| **Budgeting Tools** | "Spaces" (separate sub-accounts). You can assign virtual debit cards to Spaces for bills. | **Best-in-class.** "Pots", automated Salary Sorter, instant spend breakdown, round-ups. |
| **Social / Peer Payments** | Standard bank transfers; "Nearby Payments" to other Starling users. | **Unmatched.** Instant payments to contacts, shared tabs, and automatic bill splitting. |
| **Web / Desktop Access** | **Full web banking portal** on desktop. | Very limited emergency web access (primarily mobile app only). |
| **Account Tiers** | Strictly free (all core features included with no upsells). | Free tier, plus paid tiers (**Extra**, **Perks**, **Max**) offering insurance, credit tracker, higher ATM limits, etc. |

---

### Where Starling Wins
* **Travel outside Europe:** Starling does not limit how much cash you can withdraw fee-free from ATMs abroad (subject to their daily £300 limit), whereas Monzo’s free tier charges 3% once you exceed £200 per rolling month outside the EEA.
* **Cash & Cheque Handling:** Starling lets you deposit up to £1,000 in cash each year at any Post Office branch without a fee. Monzo charges £1 for every cash deposit on its standard free account.
* **Desktop Access:** If you prefer doing finances or checking statements on a laptop/computer screen rather than exclusively on your phone, Starling has a full desktop browser portal.
* **No Paywalled Features:** Starling gives you all of its features—including virtual cards and multi-space budgeting—for free.

### Where Monzo Wins
* **Budgeting & Day-to-Day Money Management:** Monzo’s app is more intuitive and versatile for keeping track of your monthly spend. The *Salary Sorter* automatically divides your pay into bills, savings, and spending money the moment it arrives.
* **Social Features:** If your friends, flatmates, or partner use Monzo, managing shared costs is seamless. Splitting a restaurant bill or setting up a shared tab takes seconds.
* **Bundled Perks (Paid Tiers):** If you want travel insurance, mobile phone insurance, breakdown cover, or a Greggs treat each week, Monzo’s paid tiers (Perks and Max) offer competitive packaged value.

---

### The Verdict

* **Choose Starling if:** You want a completely free primary current account, you travel frequently outside Europe, you occasionally deposit cash/cheques, or you want desktop browser access alongside the mobile app.
* **Choose Monzo if:** Your priority is daily budgeting, visualising spending habits, and easily splitting expenses with friends or flatmates who already use Monzo.

*(Tip: Because both are free to open with no minimum pay-in requirements, many UK residents hold both—using Monzo for everyday spending and social splitting, and Starling for travel and banking utility.)*
